title: Group convolutional networks for neural quantum states
scope: 3x3 torus, N9, U16.74, nmax4; exact symmetry and Adam+log-MSE qualification; no VMC

slides.title:
Group convolutional networks
for neural quantum states
slides.subtitle: 3 × 3 Bose–Hubbard torus · N = 9 · ED-first supervised study

slides.title: Four questions
lines: 1. What symmetry operators commute with the Hamiltonian?
2. Which symmetries does the finite ED ground state have?
3. How do we build those symmetries into a CNN?
4. Can Adam + log-MSE recover the remaining amplitudes?

slides.title: Our finite quantum problem
lines: $H=-t\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}(b_i^\dagger b_j+b_j^\dagger b_i)+\frac{U}{2}\sum_i n_i(n_i-1)$
t = 1; U/t = 16.74; periodic x and y; 18 unique undirected bonds.
$\mathbf{n}=(n_0,\ldots,n_8),\quad 0\leq n_i\leq4,\quad \sum_i n_i=9.$
$|\psi\rangle=\sum_{\mathbf{n}}\psi(\mathbf{n})|\mathbf{n}\rangle;\qquad i=x+3y.$
The uniform local cutoff is part of this benchmark Hamiltonian.

slides.title: What is a symmetry?
lines: An operator $U_g$ is a unitary symmetry when $U_gHU_g^{-1}=H$.
Spatial operations permute sites: $U_g|\mathbf{n}\rangle=|g\mathbf{n}\rangle$.
$(g\mathbf{n})(\mathbf{r})=\mathbf{n}(g^{-1}\mathbf{r})$: move the occupations with the sites.
A group is a set of operations closed under composition and inverses.
Commuting with H preserves an energy eigenspace; it need not fix every excited state.

slides.title: Generators of spatial symmetry
slides.subtitle: All coordinates are modulo 3. R rotates by 90°; M reflects across the x axis.

slides.title: Why the group is non-Abelian
lines: $T_xT_y=T_yT_x$, but $RT_xR^{-1}=T_y$ and $RT_yR^{-1}=T_x^{-1}$.
$MRM=R^{-1}$: a mirror and a quarter-turn do not commute.
$D_4=\{1,R,R^2,R^3,M,RM,R^2M,R^3M\}$ has 8 elements.
$G=(\mathbb{Z}_3\times\mathbb{Z}_3)\rtimes D_4$ has $9\times8=72$ elements.
The semidirect product means a rotation also changes a translation's direction.

slides.title: Internal symmetry and time reversal
slides.subtitle: Single-component bosons have no internal spin SU(2) symmetry in this model.

slides.title: Number rotations and real H
lines: $\hat N=\sum_i n_i,\qquad [H,\hat N]=0,\qquad V(\phi)=e^{i\phi\hat N}$.
$V(\phi)b_iV(\phi)^{-1}=e^{-i\phi}b_i$: hopping conserves total charge.
$G_{\rm unitary}=U(1)\times[(\mathbb{Z}_3\times\mathbb{Z}_3)\rtimes D_4]$.
$KHK^{-1}=H$: coefficients are real. K conjugates complex scalar coefficients.
There is no exact soft-boson particle–hole symmetry imposed here.

slides.title: Representations: symmetry as matrices
lines: Choose basis states $|v_1\rangle,\ldots,|v_d\rangle$ in a symmetry-invariant subspace.
$U_g|v_\alpha\rangle=\sum_{\beta=1}^{d}|v_\beta\rangle\,D_{\beta\alpha}(g)$.
$D(g_1g_2)=D(g_1)D(g_2)$: the matrices obey the same multiplication as the operators.
An irrep is an invariant subspace with no smaller nonzero invariant subspace.
A one-dimensional irrep assigns one scalar to each operator; a two-dimensional one mixes two states.

slides.title: Translations and zero momentum
lines: $T_x|\psi_{\mathbf{k}}\rangle=e^{ik_x}|\psi_{\mathbf{k}}\rangle,\quad T_y|\psi_{\mathbf{k}}\rangle=e^{ik_y}|\psi_{\mathbf{k}}\rangle$.
$k_\alpha=2\pi m_\alpha/3$, with $m_\alpha=0,1,2$, because $T_\alpha^3=I$.
$\mathbf{k}=0$ means $T_x\psi=T_y\psi=\psi$: translating the state gives no phase.
Rotations send $\mathbf{k}\mapsto R\mathbf{k}$. Zero momentum stays zero under every $R,M$.
We can therefore classify the k = 0 subspace using the full square point group D4.
slides.footer: At nonzero momentum, a rotation may connect different momentum blocks; the full-D4 labels below cannot be assigned independently to an arbitrary single momentum.

slides.title: Define A1, A2, B1, B2 and E
slides.subtitle: Within k = 0: R is the quarter-turn and M is the x-axis mirror defined earlier.
slides.footer: R and M generate all eight point-group elements. In one dimension these scalar signs define the whole irrep. The E matrices are those on the preceding example slide.

slides.title: What A1 means for our ground state
lines: $T_x|\psi_0\rangle=T_y|\psi_0\rangle=|\psi_0\rangle\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathbf{k}=0$.
$U_R|\psi_0\rangle=|\psi_0\rangle,\quad U_M|\psi_0\rangle=|\psi_0\rangle\quad\Longrightarrow\quad A_1$.
Equivalently, $\psi_0(g\mathbf{n})=\psi_0(\mathbf{n})$ for every one of the 72 spatial operations.
This is an equality of amplitudes for symmetry-related occupation configurations.
It does not set the amplitudes of different orbits. Next we check these equalities directly with ED.

slides.title: Check the operator and the state
lines: Build each site permutation and its occupation-basis permutation matrix $P_g$.
Operator test: $P_gHP_g^{-1}-H=0$ for the generators.
State test: $\epsilon_g=\|P_g\psi_{\rm ED}-\psi_{\rm ED}\|_2$ for all 72 operations.
Project onto momenta and $D_4$ irreps; check the norm of each projection.
Use the saved independently constructed ED vector; no neural predictions enter these tests.

slides.title: What is the A1 projection weight?
lines: $P_{A_1}=\frac{1}{8}\sum_{h\in D_4}U_h$ averages a state over the eight rotations/reflections.
$|\psi_{A_1}\rangle=P_{A_1}|\psi\rangle,\qquad w_{A_1}=\frac{\langle\psi|P_{A_1}|\psi\rangle}{\langle\psi|\psi\rangle}=\frac{\|\psi_{A_1}\|^2}{\|\psi\|^2}$.
The projector keeps the fully symmetric component and removes the other D4 components.
$w_{A_1}=1$ means the entire normalized state lies in A1; it is not a basis-state probability.
Similarly $P_{\mathbf{k}=0}=\frac{1}{9}\sum_{d_x,d_y=0}^2 T_x^{d_x}T_y^{d_y}$ selects translation invariance.

slides.title: ED symmetry checks
slides.footer: Exact finite-sector sums, double precision. Nonzero-momentum projector weight is about 2 × 10⁻³⁰.

slides.title: Read the ground-state observables
lines: $\rho_i=\langle\psi|n_i|\psi\rangle,\qquad C_{ij}=\langle\psi|b_i^\dagger b_j|\psi\rangle$.
$\mathcal{B}_\alpha$: the nine unique undirected nearest-neighbor bonds along axis $\alpha$.
$G_\alpha=\frac{1}{9}\sum_{(i,j)\in\mathcal{B}_\alpha}\mathrm{Re}\,C_{ij},\qquad D=\frac{1}{9}\sum_i\langle n_i(n_i-1)\rangle$.
Translation fixes $\rho_i=1$; rotations fix $G_x=G_y$.
Neither relation fixes the coherence magnitude or the onsite fluctuations D.

slides.title: One amplitude per spatial orbit
lines: An orbit $O_a$ contains all distinct configurations $g\mathbf{n}$ related by symmetry.
$\psi(g\mathbf{n})=\psi(\mathbf{n})$ fixes equality inside each orbit.
$|O_a\rangle=\frac{1}{\sqrt{m_a}}\sum_{\mathbf{n}\in O_a}|\mathbf{n}\rangle,\qquad m_a=|O_a|.$
$|\psi\rangle=\sum_a c_a|O_a\rangle,\qquad \psi(\mathbf{n}\in O_a)=c_a/\sqrt{m_a}.$
19,855 configurations → 338 orbits; orbit sizes vary from 1 to 72.

slides.title: Symmetry does not solve H
lines: Within the N = 9, k = 0 subspace, the one-dimensional A1 irrep occurs 338 times.
The invariant block is $H_{\rm inv}=S^\mathsf{T}HS$, of size $338\times338$.
$S_{\mathbf{n},a}=1/\sqrt{m_a}$ if $\mathbf{n}\in O_a$, and 0 otherwise.
We still have to determine 338 positive orbit coefficients and their normalization.
The reduced ED vector reconstructs the full state to 1.35e-15.

slides.title: Ordinary CNN: define every index
lines: $X_c(\mathbf{r})=\mathbf{1}_{n(\mathbf{r})=c},\quad c=0,1,2,3,4,\quad\mathbf{r}=(x,y)$.
$F_o(\mathbf{r})=\sigma\!\left[\beta_o+\sum_{c=0}^4\sum_{\boldsymbol{\delta}\in\Delta}K_{oc}(\boldsymbol{\delta})X_c(\mathbf{r}+\boldsymbol{\delta})\right]$.
$c$: input occupation channel; $o=1,\ldots,C$: learned output feature channel.
$\boldsymbol{\delta}=(\delta_x,\delta_y)\in\Delta=\{-1,0,1\}^2$: the nine relative positions of a 3 × 3 kernel.
$K_{oc}$: learned weights; $\beta_o$: learned bias; $\sigma(z)=z/(1+e^{-z})$: SiLU.
slides.footer: Input c labels a possible local boson number, not a species. Output o has no prescribed physical observable. Positions wrap modulo 3; the same K and β are used at every site.

slides.title: Features move; amplitudes agree
slides.footer: Example: one input/output channel, a shared periodic 3 × 3 kernel and SiLU. The group CNN will extend this consistency from translations to rotations and reflections.

slides.title: Lift to eight square orientations
slides.footer: Illustrative weights only. The actual trainable filters have input/output channels and shared biases.

slides.title: Lift: one filter, eight orientations
lines: $K^{(h)}_{oc}(\boldsymbol{\delta})=K_{oc}(h^{-1}\boldsymbol{\delta}),\qquad h\in D_4$.
$F_o^{(1)}(\mathbf{r},h)=\sigma\!\left[\beta_o+\sum_{c=0}^4\sum_{\boldsymbol{\delta}\in\Delta}K^{(h)}_{oc}(\boldsymbol{\delta})X_c(\mathbf{r}+\boldsymbol{\delta})\right]$.
$X_c,\mathbf{r},c,o,\Delta$ are the ordinary-CNN inputs and indices defined above.
New index $h$ specifies the filter orientation; $h^{-1}\boldsymbol{\delta}$ rotates/reflects its relative coordinates.
Example: $h=R$, $\boldsymbol{\delta}=(1,0)$ gives $h^{-1}\boldsymbol{\delta}=(0,-1)$.
slides.footer: All orientations share K and β. Superscript (1) denotes the first layer. Each output channel now has eight spatial response maps, rather than one.

slides.title: Rotations move maps and labels
slides.footer: Here g = (t,q) maps a site r to t + q r; t is a translation and q is a D4 rotation/reflection. The diagram uses q = R, t = 0 and the same illustrative scalar filter as before.

slides.title: Group convolution: mix orientations
lines: $F_o^{(2)}(\mathbf{r},h)=\sigma\!\left[\gamma_o+\sum_{p=1}^{C}\sum_{a\in D_4}\sum_{\boldsymbol{\delta}\in\Delta}W_{op}(h^{-1}\boldsymbol{\delta},h^{-1}a)F_p^{(1)}(\mathbf{r}+\boldsymbol{\delta},a)\right]$.
$p$: input learned feature channel; $o$: output learned feature channel (both 1 to C = 16 here).
$a$: input orientation; $h$: output orientation; $\gamma_o$: shared learned bias.
$W_{op}(\boldsymbol{\epsilon},s)$: learned kernel with relative position $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}=h^{-1}\boldsymbol{\delta}$ and orientation $s=h^{-1}a$.
Each output map combines all eight input orientations, with the same relative-coordinate rule.
slides.footer: The occupation channel c is only used in the input/lifting layer. Hidden-layer channels use p and o. W has shape (16,16,8,3,3); γ has 16 entries.

slides.title: The complete group CNN
slides.footer: wₒ and η are learned readout weights and bias. Zθ is the sum of exp(2fθ) over all N = 9 configurations; it normalizes the state.

slides.title: Adam + log-MSE in the fixed sector
lines: $\ell_\theta(\mathbf{n})=f_\theta(\mathbf{n})-\frac{1}{2}\log Z_\theta,\quad Z_\theta=\sum_{\mathbf{n}\in\mathcal{H}_9}e^{2f_\theta(\mathbf{n})}$.
$\mathcal{L}=\frac{1}{19855}\sum_{\mathbf{n}\in\mathcal{H}_9}[\ell_\theta(\mathbf{n})-\log\psi_{\rm ED}(\mathbf{n})]^2$.
Using 338 orbit representatives $\mathbf{n}_a$ with sizes $m_a$ gives exactly the same loss:
$Z_\theta=\sum_a m_ae^{2f_\theta(\mathbf{n}_a)},\quad\mathcal{L}=\sum_a\frac{m_a}{19855}[\ell_\theta(\mathbf{n}_a)-\log\psi_{\rm ED}(\mathbf{n}_a)]^2$.
Optimize with Adam; check $F=|\langle\psi_\theta|\psi_{\rm ED}\rangle|$ and physical observables afterwards.
slides.footer: ℓθ is the normalized log amplitude; H₉ is the N = 9 configuration basis. Each orbit representative nₐ carries its orbit size mₐ.

slides.title: One predeclared training run
rows: C = 16; one lift + one group conv + linear head
Lowest log-MSE; final direct full-basis CPU float64 check
slides.footer: No infidelity minimization, energy selection, architecture grid or early stopping. All 338 orbit representatives carry their multiplicities.

slides.title: Adam learns the orbit amplitudes
slides.footer: Curves are snapshots every 100 updates. Red line: selected update 10000; selection checks log-MSE after every update, not only plotted snapshots.

slides.title: Selected checkpoint against ED
slides.footer: Direct evaluation of all 19,855 configurations. The earlier tiny-system gate (F ≥ 0.9999 AND ΔE/site ≤ 0.001t) does not pass; the agreed 3×3 working gate is F ≥ 0.99.

slides.title: Check amplitudes across all orbits
slides.footer: One point per spatial orbit (338 points). Histogram also counts orbits, not configurations; the training MSE instead weights each orbit by its multiplicity.

slides.title: Symmetry survives training
slides.footer: Independent checks also compare literal coordinate convolution sums, all 72 feature/output transformations, input gradients, parameter gradients and checkpoint round trips.

slides.title: Symmetry fixes relations, not values
slides.footer: These are exhaustive fixed-sector expectations, not Monte Carlo measurements. Correlation magnitudes and D test learned dynamics; density and Gx = Gy also follow from imposed symmetry.

slides.title: Earlier fits: numerical context
slides.footer: Historical runs: same 3×3 N = 9 cutoff-4 physics, Adam/log-MSE, seed 123, 10,000 updates. Widths, parameter counts, arithmetic and implementations differ. This is not a controlled architecture ranking.

slides.title: Conclusion: build symmetry into NQS
lines: The ED ground state is unchanged by translations, square rotations and reflections.
The group CNN makes these equalities exact by sharing filters over orientations.
Symmetry fixes relations between amplitudes; training learns the different orbit weights.
Adam + log-MSE reaches overlap 0.9996089 on the 3 × 3, N = 9 torus.

slides.title: Why the finite ground state is symmetric
lines: Hopping gives nonpositive off-diagonal matrix elements in the occupation basis.
The fixed-N configuration graph is connected for t > 0.
Perron–Frobenius: its ground state is unique and can be strictly positive.
A site permutation must produce the same positive, normalized ground vector.
Therefore: charge $9$, momentum $\mathbf{k}=0$, spatial irrep $A_1$, and $K\psi=\psi$.
slides.footer: Finite canonical sector only. This does not identify the grand-canonical sector at μ = 0 or prove bulk symmetry breaking.

slides.title: Pooling: the invariance proof
lines: $z_c=\frac{1}{9\times8}\sum_{\mathbf{r},h}F_c^{(2)}(\mathbf{r},h),\qquad f_\theta(\mathbf{n})=\mathrm{head}(z)$.
A group operation only permutes the terms in this average.
Thus $f_\theta(g\mathbf{n})=f_\theta(\mathbf{n})$ for any learned weights.
$\psi_\theta(\mathbf{n})=e^{f_\theta(\mathbf{n})}/\sqrt{Z_\theta}$ is real, positive and spatially A1.
Particle number is separate: normalize and train only inside the N = 9 sector.

slides.title: Scope of the ansatz
lines: Built in: translations, quarter-turns, reflections, and positive real amplitudes.
Learned: the different orbit weights, fluctuations and coherence magnitudes.
Not built in: zero amplitude in other particle sectors; project explicitly when needed.
On 3 × 3 a 3 × 3 kernel already covers the whole torus.
This tiny ED study tests correctness and representation, not large-system scaling.

slides.title: Orbit reduction: implementation checks
lines: $Z_\theta=\sum_{a=1}^{338}m_a e^{2f_\theta(\mathbf{n}_a)}$.
$\mathcal{L}=\sum_a\frac{m_a}{19855}[f_\theta(\mathbf{n}_a)-\frac{1}{2}\log Z_\theta-\log\psi_{\rm ED}(\mathbf{n}_a)]^2$.
Exact invariance lets us evaluate one representative per orbit during training.
The multiplicities mₐ preserve the full-basis normalization and MSE weighting.
This is an exact computational reduction, not a new loss or Monte Carlo estimate.
slides.footer: Enable this reduction only after independent invariance checks; compare both loss and gradients to the full-basis calculation.

slides.title: Finite-size and critical-point notes
lines: U/t = 16.74 is motivated by the bulk unit-filling critical region.
This 3 × 3, cutoff-4 torus has a neutral fixed-N ED gap of 9.015297 t.
A bulk gapless limit does not make this finite canonical problem gapless.
This study tests supervised representation; it makes no VMC or bulk critical-scaling claim.
Larger sizes, cutoff convergence and optimization robustness require separate studies.
slides.footer: Bulk reference: Capogrosso-Sansone et al., Phys. Rev. A 77, 015602 (2008), doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.77.015602; reported (t/U)c = 0.05974(3).

slides.title: D4 characters at zero momentum
slides.footer: Class sizes: 1, 2, 1, 2, 2. At nonzero momentum, use the momentum little group and its star; arbitrary momentum/D4 pairs are not independent labels.

slides.title: Projectors used in the ED audit
lines: $P_{\mathbf{k}}=\frac{1}{9}\sum_{d_x,d_y=0}^2 e^{-i\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{d}}T_x^{d_x}T_y^{d_y}$.
$P_\lambda=\frac{d_\lambda}{8}\sum_{h\in D_4}\chi_\lambda(h)^*U_h$.
Report projection weights $\|P\psi_{\rm ED}\|^2$, not individual basis-state probabilities.
The complete projector norms sum to 1 within floating-point precision.
Complex conjugation K is antiunitary; it is checked separately, not inserted in these unitary sums.

slides.title: Count orbits without guessing
lines: Burnside: $\#\mathrm{orbits}=\frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}\#\{\mathbf{n}:g\mathbf{n}=\mathbf{n}\}$.
A site permutation decomposes into cycles. A fixed configuration is constant on each cycle.
For a cycle of length $s$, the occupancy generating polynomial is $\sum_{n=0}^{4}z^{sn}$.
Multiply over cycles and read the coefficient of $z^9$; sum over all 72 operations.
Result: 24,336 / 72 = 338 orbits, independently checked against explicit orbit enumeration.

slides.title: Why the group layer is equivariant
lines: Let $g=(\mathbf{t},q)$, with $q\in D_4$ and translation $\mathbf{t}$; $g\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{t}+q\mathbf{r}$.
The input field transforms as $F'_p(\mathbf{r},a)=F_p(q^{-1}(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{t}),q^{-1}a)$.
In the convolution, substitute $\boldsymbol{\delta}'=q^{-1}\boldsymbol{\delta}$, $a'=q^{-1}a$, $h'=q^{-1}h$.
Then $h^{-1}\boldsymbol{\delta}=(h')^{-1}\boldsymbol{\delta}'$ and $h^{-1}a=(h')^{-1}a'$.

The sum is the original output at the transformed site and orientation.
Shared biases and SiLU preserve this equality.

slides.title: Observables: exact sector sums
lines: $\langle n_i\rangle=\sum_{\mathbf{n}}|\psi(\mathbf{n})|^2n_i$.
$\langle b_i^\dagger b_j\rangle=\sum_{\mathbf{n}}\psi^*(\mathbf{n}+\mathbf{e}_i-\mathbf{e}_j)\psi(\mathbf{n})\sqrt{(n_i+1)n_j}$ for $i\ne j$.
Include only allowed hops: nⱼ > 0 and nᵢ < cutoff. The diagonal equals the density.
All benchmark observables here enumerate the 19,855-state sector; no sampling errors.
For future MC, average the corresponding amplitude-ratio local estimator and account for autocorrelation.
